summary: Split the C# test suite off the live playtest-editable Lion/Crane deck (issue #115). New frozen scenario PublishedContent.TestSnapshot/MatchEngine.CreatePublishedTestMatch() (content/published/lion-crane-test-v1.json, one-time copy of today's pinned deck lists, never auto-regenerated) is used by PublishedTests.cs's generic-mechanics tests and Program.cs's BowedPersonalityResolution; PublishedContent.Snapshot/CreatePublishedMatch() stays exactly what it is today, the live app deck, freely editable for playtesting going forward. Its own Cards are deliberately not merged into CardCatalog, avoiding a duplicate-id conflict -- only the deck lists are pinned, card behavior still resolves through the one shared CardCatalog. A few tests (OfferedActions, Replay) deliberately keep exercising the live deck as smoke tests. Also restored Ikoma Takakura and Doji Tatsuki -- cut from the live deck in #114 -- to VanillaWave1 rather than leaving them silently deleted from CardCatalog entirely, per the user's explicit 'never delete a card unless told it's not Emperor-legal' policy; verified their source scan hashes against the untouched originals before restoring. Recorded the policy in docs/decisions/2026-09-09-test-live-deck-split.md. Shared-file change: touches src/L5R.Client/Content/Published only to restore two cards' scanned artwork, no client code changed; all other changes are rules-lane engine-only.
validation: bash tools/check.sh --skip-client: 85/85 core tests, 33/33 published tests (2 new TestSnapshot structural checks in Catalogue, vanilla-wave-1 count 61->63, total published 122->124), 8/8 deck-format, plus AI/server/client-transport checks -- all pass.
remaining: This is a starting point per the user's direction -- client (Godot) and RoomManager's scenario gating are untouched, to evolve once the full application is tested more robustly.
